theme: Endosomal nucleic-acid-sensing TLRs and their inborn errors
story: The centre is the endosomal Toll-like receptors (TLR3, TLR7, TLR8, TLR9) that sense viral and self nucleic acids: their UNC93B1-dependent trafficking and processing, positive and negative regulation, and SLC15A4:TASL-driven IRF5 activation. The herpes simplex encephalitis entries (UNC93B1, TLR3, TICAM1/TRIF, TRAF3 deficiency) are the human genetic proof that this TLR3-TRIF-TRAF3 axis is needed for antiviral interferon in the brain. TREX1 regulation and defective TLR7 control by endogenous ligand, together with the TLR8-BAFF network, show the other side: when self nucleic acids are not cleared, these sensors drive autoimmunity. The cluster as a whole is about endosomal nucleic acid sensing, balancing antiviral defence against self-reactivity.

theme: Heme biosynthesis and systemic iron homeostasis
story: At the centre is heme synthesis (the porphyrin pathway through protoporphyrinogen to heme B and heme A) and its regulation, which drives hemoglobin production. Around it sits the iron supply chain: transferrin endocytosis and recycling, iron import, ferroportin (SLC40A1), DMT1 (SLC11A2) and ceruloplasmin defects causing hemochromatosis, anemia or aceruloplasminemia, plus heme scavenging and transport, and the mitochondrial ABC transporters and cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly that share mitochondrial iron. Together the cluster describes how the body takes up, moves and uses iron to build heme and hemoglobin.

theme: Glycan synthesis, glycosylation and lysosomal glycan breakdown
story: The core is protein and lipid glycosylation: making nucleotide sugars (UDP-GlcNAc, GDP-mannose, GDP-fucose, CMP-sialic acid, UDP-glucuronate), moving them into the Golgi through SLC35 transporters, then building N-glycans, O-glycans, GPI anchors, glycosphingolipids, gangliosides and blood-group antigens. The many congenital disorders of glycosylation (ALG6, ALG14, MOGS, MAN1B1, SLC35A1/A2/C1, GNE, GALNT3, C1GALT1C1) show what happens when these steps fail. The other side of the cycle is lysosomal targeting and breakdown of glycans and glycolipids (HEXA/HEXB GM2 gangliosidoses, NEU1 sialidosis, Salla disease), and the selectin-ligand items (leukocyte rolling, stem cell homing) show what these glycans do. The whole cluster is the glycan life cycle from sugar activation through assembly to lysosomal turnover; a few members (chitin, paranodal junction, peptidyl-tyrosine modification) are only loosely attached.

theme: Peroxisomal fatty acid beta-oxidation
story: The centre is peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very long chain and branched fatty acids (acyl-CoA oxidase pathway, pristanoyl-CoA oxidation), with ABCD1 importing the substrates; its defect causes adrenoleukodystrophy. Peroxisome fission and TYSND1 protease processing of peroxisomal enzymes keep the organelle itself working. The medium- and long-chain acyl-CoA, malonyl-CoA and succinyl-CoA items describe the fatty acyl-CoA handling that feeds into and follows this pathway, so the cluster as a whole is about the peroxisome as a fatty-acid-breaking organelle.

theme: Cytosolic nucleic acid sensing to type I interferon
story: The centre is the cytosolic detection of viral RNA and DNA: RIG-I and DEx/H-box helicases sense double-stranded RNA, the cytosolic DNA sensing pathway senses DNA, and both signal through IRF3 to induce type I interferon. The downstream items (interferon-alpha response, OAS antiviral response, IP-10 production, activated dendritic cells) show what that interferon does to cells. Together the cluster describes the cell-intrinsic innate antiviral response, from sensing to interferon to antiviral effectors.

theme: Fc gamma receptor activating and inhibitory signaling
story: The centre is Fc receptor signaling by IgG: FCGR activation driving antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and acute inflammation, opposed by inhibitory Fc receptor signaling. Signal regulatory protein (SIRP) interactions and negative regulation of phagocytosis and neutrophil activation add the don't-eat-me and dampening controls, and type II hypersensitivity shows the disease consequence. The cluster is about how antibody-coated targets trigger myeloid effector function and how that response is kept in check.

theme: Kidney nephron development
story: The centre is metanephric kidney development: the ureteric bud grows and branches and induces the metanephric mesenchyme to undergo mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition, forming renal vesicles, comma-shaped and S-shaped bodies that pattern into nephron tubules and the distal convoluted tubule. Earlier stages (intermediate mesoderm, nephric duct, pronephros) set up the tissue, and the regulators of stem/progenitor maintenance, proliferation, apoptosis and kidney size control how many nephrons form. The cluster as a whole describes how the nephron is built from embryonic mesoderm.

theme: Myeloid inflammatory cytokine response and its restraint
story: The centre is activation of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells through NF-kB to produce proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines, captured by the hallmark inflammatory response and myeloid activation modules. The many negative regulation terms (IL-8, MCP-1, CXCL2, macrophage cytokines, inflammation to wounding, chronic inflammation) are the brakes on the same output. Together the cluster describes myeloid-driven inflammation as a balance between cytokine induction and its suppression.

theme: Plasma lipoprotein remodeling and clearance
story: The centre is the life of plasma lipoproteins after secretion: VLDL assembly, remodeling of HDL and LDL particles, and the clearance of chylomicrons, VLDL, LDL and other triglyceride-rich particles by the liver. Phosphatidylcholine catabolism and phospholipid regulation reflect the lipase and LCAT steps that remodel particle surfaces, while cholesterol import, storage and lipoprotein signaling describe what cells do with the delivered lipid. The cluster is about how lipids are transported in blood and taken up by tissues.

theme: ESCRT-mediated membrane scission and budding
story: The centre is the ESCRT machinery, which bends and cuts membranes away from the cytosol: it builds multivesicular bodies, sorts ubiquitinated receptors such as EGFR for lysosomal degradation, and is recycled by ESCRT disassembly. The same fission machinery seals the nuclear envelope, releases exosomes, and is hijacked by enveloped viruses such as HIV (GAG targeting, virion budding, non-lytic release); Listeria InlB entry adds ubiquitin-dependent receptor endocytosis. The cluster describes one membrane-fission system and the cellular and viral processes that use it.

theme: Centrosome positioning and microtubule/actomyosin organization
story: The centre is the centrosome as microtubule organizing centre: centriole cohesion, microtubule nucleation and anchoring, stabilization of microtubules, and moving and holding the centrosome in place. Rho GTPase signaling (Rho cycle, CIT activation), actomyosin contractile ring and septin ring organization, and cortical protein localization describe the actin-based cortex that partners with microtubules. Together the cluster is about how cells position their cytoskeleton, for polarity and for cytokinesis.

theme: Cellular energy buffering, magnesium and small-molecule housekeeping
story: The most coherent part is cellular energy handling: creatine and phosphocreatine metabolism buffer ATP, mitochondrial ADP/ATP exchange moves it, and magnesium transport and homeostasis matter because ATP works as a Mg-ATP complex. Other members are only loosely related: PRPP synthesis, inositol metabolism and transport, fructose biosynthesis, and generic protein homo- and hetero-oligomerization and calcium-independent adhesion. As a whole the cluster is a weakly unified collection of metabolic housekeeping processes with energy and Mg-ATP at its centre.

theme: NOTCH1 signaling and its oncogenic activation
story: The centre is canonical NOTCH1 signaling: the activated receptor releases its intracellular domain, which moves to the nucleus to regulate transcription, with NOTCH2 activation as a parallel paralog. Most other members are cancer mutations that make the pathway constitutively active (HD-domain, PEST-domain and translocation mutants, loss of the FBXW7 ubiquitin ligase that normally degrades NICD), as in T-cell leukemia, and negative regulation of Notch signaling and the hallmark set frame the normal controls. The cluster is about Notch signal transmission and how its loss of control drives cancer.

theme: Notch transcriptional output
story: The centre is what Notch does in the nucleus: the NOTCH1 intracellular domain activates transcription of target genes, notably the HES/HEY bHLH repressors (Notch-HLH pathway). Constitutively active NOTCH1 PEST and HD+PEST mutants show this output stuck on in cancer, and negative regulation of Notch signaling provides the brake. The cluster as a whole is Notch-driven gene regulation.

theme: GPCR control of pancreatic islet hormone secretion
story: The centre is regulation of insulin and glucagon secretion by G-protein-coupled receptors: GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, GPR40 free fatty acid receptors and acetylcholine raise secretion through adenylate cyclase and cAMP/PKA, while adrenaline/noradrenaline and somatostatin inhibit it. Related peptide receptor families (calcitonin-like, CGRP, amylin, hydroxycarboxylic acid receptors) and growth hormone secretion extend the picture to other hormone-secreting cells using the same cAMP logic. The cluster is about how nutrients and hormones tune endocrine secretion through GPCR-cAMP signaling.

theme: Postsynaptic actin and dendritic spine plasticity
story: The centre is the actin cytoskeleton of the postsynapse: organizing and modifying postsynaptic actin, maintaining the postsynaptic density, and assembling postsynaptic structures. Filopodium regulation, RHOF signaling and negative regulation of spine and dendrite development describe the Rho-GTPase-driven shape changes, and delivery of neurotransmitter receptors from endosomes to the postsynaptic membrane adds the functional side. Together the cluster describes structural synaptic plasticity, where spine shape and receptor content change together.

theme: Type 2 immunity: Th2 cells, eosinophils and mast cells
story: The centre is Th2 differentiation of naive CD4 T cells and their cytokines IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, with both positive and negative regulation of their production and signaling. Downstream, IL-5 and related signals drive eosinophil differentiation, migration, activation and effector function, and mast cell differentiation and activation complete the effector arm, with granulocyte differentiation (G-CSF) as supporting myelopoiesis. Response to nematodes names the physiological purpose: the whole cluster is the type 2 immune response against helminths, which also underlies allergy.

theme: SLC anion and proton transporters, pH and mineralization
story: The centre is transport of inorganic anions and protons: bicarbonate transporters (SLC4), SLC26 anion exchangers for chloride, sulfate, oxalate and iodide, sodium/proton exchangers, carbonic anhydrase-driven CO2 hydration, and phosphate transport, which together set pH. Most other members are disease variants of these carriers (renal tubular acidosis, spherocytosis, Pendred syndrome, chloride diarrhea, autism and X-linked intellectual disability, basal ganglia calcification) and the processes that depend on them, especially enamel mineralization, tooth eruption, and calcification disorders such as PXE. The cluster is about ion and pH handling by solute carriers and how its failure shows up in kidney, gut, blood and mineralized tissue.

theme: Endosomal TLR7/8/9 signaling in dendritic cells
story: The centre is endosomal Toll-like receptors 7, 8 and 9, which detect nucleic acids, with their positive and negative regulation and SLC15A4:TASL-dependent IRF5 activation. The output is dendritic cell activation and cytokine production, and DEx/H-box helicase signaling adds a parallel cytosolic route to type I interferon and inflammatory cytokines. The cluster describes how dendritic cells turn nucleic acid sensing into cytokine responses.

theme: Amino acid catabolism and its vitamin cofactors
story: The centre is breakdown and interconversion of amino acids: phenylalanine and tyrosine (with phenylketonuria), serine, glycine and threonine, histidine and proline, and the transsulfuration route from homocysteine to cysteine and on to hydrogen sulfide and sulfate. The cofactors these enzymes need form the second layer: tetrahydrobiopterin for phenylalanine hydroxylase, vitamin B6 (pyridoxal phosphate) for most transaminases and transsulfuration, and the molybdenum cofactor for sulfite oxidation. Formate, glyoxylate and pyrimidine catabolism are linked one-carbon and nitrogen side branches, so the cluster as a whole describes amino acid catabolism together with the cofactors that make it run.

theme: RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signaling and its oncogenic mutants
story: The centre is the MAPK cascade: SOS activates RAS, RAS activates RAF, RAF activates MAP2K, which activates ERK and then RSK, with RAS GAPs (including NF1) and the SHOC2-MRAS complex controlling the entry point. Many members are cancer and RASopathy variants that hyperactivate this cascade (BRAF high- and moderate-activity and kinase-dead paradoxical mutants, RAF fusions, RAF1, MAP2K and MAPK mutants, NF1 loss). Negative feedback, ERK dephosphorylation by phosphatases and negative regulation of RAS and ERK form the brakes, so the cluster describes the ERK pathway as a whole: activation, mutational hyperactivation, and shut-off.

theme: Urea cycle and nitrogen metabolism
story: The centre is the urea cycle, in which ornithine, citrulline and arginine carry ammonia nitrogen into urea, with the mitochondrial ornithine carrier SLC25A15 (HHH syndrome) and transcriptional control of the cycle enzymes. Feeding it is glutamate, glutamine and aspartate metabolism, which collect and hand over nitrogen through 2-oxoglutarate and transamination, and ammonium homeostasis and response to ammonium describe the goal. The cluster as a whole is about how the body handles and disposes of amino acid nitrogen.

theme: Death receptor-mediated extrinsic apoptosis
story: The centre is extrinsic apoptosis triggered by death receptors: Fas ligand and TRAIL bind their receptors, procaspase-8 dimerizes and activates, and caspase-8 cleaves BID, which moves to mitochondria to amplify the death signal. c-FLIP and other caspase-8 inhibition, and negative regulation of Fas and TNF signaling, are the brakes, while T-cell activation-induced death, thymocyte apoptosis and hepatocyte apoptosis are the settings where this pathway matters. The cluster describes receptor-triggered cell death and how it is controlled.

theme: DNA double-strand break sensing and repair pathway choice
story: The centre is the response to a DNA double-strand break: sensing the break, ATM-driven phosphorylation and recruitment of repair proteins, ADP-ribosylation and chromatin remodeling at the site. The break is then repaired by classical or alternative non-homologous end joining or by homologous recombination, and the paired positive and negative regulators of each route describe how the cell chooses between them. The cluster as a whole is about double-strand break repair and its pathway choice.

theme: GPCR regulation of insulin and glucagon secretion
story: The centre is control of pancreatic islet hormone release by G-protein-coupled receptors: GLP-1, glucagon, acetylcholine and fatty acids via GPR40 stimulate insulin secretion, with adenylate cyclase activation as the shared cAMP mechanism. Somatostatin signaling and negative regulation of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion are the inhibitory side, and growth hormone secretion is a related endocrine output. The cluster is about how hormones and nutrients tune islet hormone output.

theme: Deoxyribonucleotide synthesis, salvage and catabolism
story: The centre is the metabolism of DNA building blocks: synthesis of deoxyribonucleotides (dTTP and other dNTPs), pyrimidine salvage, and breakdown of deoxynucleosides and dNMPs. ADA and PNP deficiencies are the clinical anchor: failure to degrade deoxyadenosine and deoxyguanosine lets toxic dNTPs build up in lymphocytes and causes immunodeficiency. The cluster describes how cells keep their dNTP pool balanced by making, salvaging and clearing deoxynucleotides.

theme: Chondrocyte differentiation and endochondral bone formation
story: The centre is the chondrocyte life cycle: mesenchymal condensation, chondroblast differentiation, proliferation and then hypertrophy in the growth plate, driven partly by RUNX2, leading to replacement of cartilage by bone. Positive and negative regulators of chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation pace this program, while articular cartilage, joint morphogenesis and cartilage homeostasis describe the cartilage that is kept rather than replaced. The cluster is about how cartilage builds the skeleton and its joints.

theme: TGF-beta superfamily SMAD signaling and its cancer mutants
story: The centre is TGF-beta superfamily signaling through SMADs: TGF-beta, activin, BMP and anti-Mullerian hormone receptors phosphorylate SMAD2/3 or SMAD1/5, which partner with SMAD4 to regulate transcription, with positive and negative regulators, follistatin antagonism of activin, and TGFBR3 as a co-receptor. Many members are cancer mutants that break the pathway (TGFBR1/2 mutants, SMAD2/3 and SMAD4 MH2 mutants), consistent with its tumour-suppressor role, and RUNX3 targets (BIM, p21, p14-ARF) show that growth-inhibitory output. The cluster describes TGF-beta family signaling as a whole, including how cancers escape it; glycoprotein hormones and TCF7L2 mutants are loose additions.

theme: Cadherin-based cell-cell adhesion and junctions
story: The centre is cadherin-mediated, calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion, with E-cadherin (CDH1) trafficking, processing and degradation and CDH11 interactions as the specific players. Generic junction and membrane sets and the apical junction hallmark describe the structures built, and apoptotic cleavage of adhesion proteins shows how they are taken apart when cells die. The cluster is about forming and maintaining adherens junctions between cells.

theme: Lipase-driven lipoprotein remodeling and clearance
story: The centre is lipoprotein remodeling by lipases: assembling active lipoprotein lipase and hepatic lipase complexes, which hydrolyse triglycerides and phospholipids in chylomicrons and VLDL, turning them into remnants and LDL and reshaping HDL. Clearance of chylomicrons, VLDL, LDL and triglyceride-rich particles, plus VLDL assembly at the start, complete the loop. The cluster describes how dietary and liver-made fats are delivered to tissues through lipoprotein processing in blood.

theme: LDL receptor degradation and control of cholesterol uptake
story: The centre is the fate of lipoprotein receptors such as LDLR and VLDLR: their internalization, reduced recycling and lysosomal degradation, which lower LDL clearance. The LXR (NR1H2/NR1H3) pathway that limits cholesterol uptake, via IDOL-mediated receptor degradation, ties this to cellular cholesterol sensing. The cluster is about how cells regulate cholesterol import by controlling receptor abundance.

theme: Catecholamine reuptake and vesicular transport
story: The centre is the norepinephrine transmitter cycle: loading into synaptic vesicles, release, and reuptake by the norepinephrine transporter SLC6A2, whose defect causes orthostatic intolerance. Generic monoamine, catecholamine and dopamine transport terms and SLC-mediated neurotransmitter transport frame the same transporter families. The cluster is about how monoaminergic synapses recycle their transmitters.

theme: C-type lectin receptor antifungal innate immunity
story: The centre is recognition of fungi and other microbes by C-type lectin receptors: Dectin-1 (CLEC7A) signaling to NFAT and the inflammasome, the Dectin-2 family, and DC-SIGN, with response to fungal molecules, lectins and protozoa as the triggers. The outputs are cytokines that shape the immune response: IL-12, IL-23, interferon-gamma and GM-CSF for Th1/Th17 defence, balanced by IL-10 and anti-inflammatory signals (FCGR3A, ADORA2B). The cluster describes how myeloid cells sense fungal and parasite surfaces and choose an inflammatory or regulatory cytokine program.

theme: Cytochrome P450-driven xenobiotic and toxin metabolism (drug detoxification)
story: At the centre are the general xenobiotic metabolism and catabolism pathways, made concrete by specific cytochrome P450 reactions: CYP2E1 oxidations, CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation and N-dealkylation of aromatic amines, and oxidative demethylation. These Phase I oxidations work together with Phase II conjugation such as N-acetylation. Worked examples show the double-edged result: paracetamol ADME and aflatoxin activation and detoxification can each produce reactive, toxic intermediates or safe products depending on the route taken, and the same enzymes also break down plant- and fungus-derived compounds (alkaloids, monoterpenoids, phenylpropanoids, mycotoxins) and nitrogen-containing toxins. Taken together, the cluster describes the body's chemical-defence system for clearing foreign compounds from drugs, diet and the environment.

theme: Host-pathogen interactions with toxins and protozoa
story: The cluster gathers how host cells handle pathogens and their products: bacterial toxin uptake (diphtheria, anthrax), Leishmania and other protozoa, SARS therapeutics, and the GBP and NADPH oxidase defences. Most of the cytokine members describe the macrophage and dendritic cell response, with IL-12 and antigen presentation on one side and anti-inflammatory IL-10 programs (FCGR3A, CD163, ADORA2B, DC-SIGN, WNT5 damping) on the other. It is a loosely joined collection centred on infection and the myeloid response to it, rather than one pathway.

theme: Mitotic chromosome segregation and cytokinesis
story: The centre is mitosis: chromosome condensation, centromere (CENP-A) assembly and sister chromatid cohesion and its resolution, spindle assembly and orientation driven by centrosomes, Aurora A, PLK1 and NEK kinases, and the spindle checkpoint that waits for kinetochore attachment. The final stage is cytokinesis: spindle midzone, Rho-driven actomyosin ring, cleavage furrow and midbody abscission. The cluster as a whole describes the machinery that divides one cell into two with faithful chromosome segregation.

theme: HDL biogenesis and cholesterol efflux
story: The centre is reverse cholesterol transport: ABCA1 moves cellular cholesterol onto apolipoprotein A-I to assemble HDL, and its defect causes Tangier disease. Positive and negative regulators of efflux, apoA-I signaling, cellular response to cholesterol and sterol homeostasis describe how cells decide when to export cholesterol, and HDL clearance completes the route to the liver. The cluster is about removing excess cholesterol from cells via HDL.

theme: Mitochondrial respiratory complex III and IV assembly
story: The centre is assembly of the respiratory chain complexes III and IV and their combination into respirasomes. Protein insertion into the inner mitochondrial membrane provides the subunits these complexes are built from. The cluster describes building the oxidative phosphorylation machinery in the mitochondrial inner membrane.

theme: Nucleotide and NAD(P) energy currency interconversion
story: The centre is keeping the cell's energy and redox currencies in balance: interconversion of nucleoside mono-, di- and triphosphates (ADP, GTP), creatine/phosphocreatine buffering, and mitochondrial ADP/ATP exchange. NAD+ and NADP+ synthesis by nicotinate metabolism and salvage, NAD consumption and NAD transport add the redox currency. The cluster describes how cells make and redistribute the small nucleotides that power and balance metabolism.

theme: Synaptic glutamate transport and recycling
story: The centre is glutamate handling at the synapse: excitatory amino acid transporters (SLC1A1, SLC1A3) clear glutamate and aspartate from the cleft, astrocytes convert it to glutamine and send it back, and vesicular glutamate transporters with vesicle acidification reload it into vesicles. Disease variants (episodic ataxia, schizophrenia and aminoaciduria, deafness) show the consequences of failure. The cluster describes the glutamate-glutamine cycle that keeps excitatory transmission running and safe.

theme: ERK activation and feedback inactivation
story: The centre is activation of ERK1 and ERK2 (MAPK3 and MAPK1) and their downstream RSK, plus MAPK mutants that keep this on. The rest is the off-switch: phosphatases that dephosphorylate threonine and tyrosine on ERK, negative feedback of the MAPK pathway, and negative regulation of RAS and ERK signaling. The cluster describes ERK signaling as a balance between activation and feedback shutdown.

theme: Heart and cardiac outflow morphogenesis
story: The centre is building the heart wall: ventricular trabeculation and compaction, atrial and left ventricular muscle formation, and cardiomyocyte development and proliferation. The endocardium and mesenchyme form the aortic and pulmonary valves, and coronary vasculogenesis, cardiac smooth muscle and ascending aorta development build the vessels. The cluster describes embryonic heart morphogenesis from muscle to valves to vessels.

theme: DNA double-strand break repair and BRCA-dependent recombination
story: The centre is homologous recombination repair: sensing and resecting breaks, RAD51 loading by BRCA2-PALB2-BRCA1, strand invasion, and D-loop resolution through synthesis-dependent strand annealing or Holliday junctions, with single-strand annealing and NHEJ/MMEJ as alternative routes. Many members are cancer-relevant defects in BRCA1, BARD1, BRCA2 and PALB2, and the Fanconi anemia, interstrand cross-link, replication fork reversal, protein-DNA cross-link and PARP (ADP-ribosylation) items show the related repair of replication-blocking lesions. The cluster as a whole is about repairing double-strand breaks and stalled forks, and how its loss underlies hereditary cancer.

theme: Rab/ARF-regulated endosomal recycling and membrane tubulation
story: The centre is endosomal sorting and recycling: endosomes form tubules that carry receptors back to the plasma membrane, regulated by Rab GTPases and their TBC/RabGAPs and by ARF signaling. Golgi vesicle budding, Golgi membrane localization and constitutive secretion connect this to the secretory route, and plasma membrane to endosome transport supplies the cargo. The cluster describes small-GTPase control of membrane traffic between endosomes, Golgi and cell surface.

theme: Myelin, glial responses and axon growth inhibition
story: The centre is the central nervous system myelin: oligodendrocyte progenitor proliferation, myelin formation and maintenance, and regulation of myelination. Myelin-associated inhibitors signal through RHOA and ceramide to block axon growth and regeneration, set against axonal growth stimulation, and reactive gliosis and glial proliferation and migration describe the glial injury response. The cluster describes how glia build myelin and how myelin and glia limit axon regrowth after injury.

theme: Osmotic and sodium/potassium transport regulation
story: The centre is regulation of sodium and potassium movement across membranes, especially renal sodium transport under aldosterone control and the regulation of sodium and potassium import and export. Hypotonic and hyperosmotic responses and osmosensing describe the cellular volume challenge this transport answers, and transepithelial chloride transport and pancreatic secretion extend it to epithelia. The cluster is about how cells and epithelia control salt movement to balance volume and osmolarity.

theme: ER-Golgi vesicle trafficking via COPII and COPI
story: The centre is the early secretory pathway: COPII coats load cargo and bud vesicles from ER exit sites to carry proteins to the Golgi. COPI vesicles return escaped ER proteins from the Golgi back to the ER and also move cargo within the Golgi. The cluster describes the two-way vesicle traffic between ER and Golgi.

theme: Amino acid and thyroid hormone membrane transport
story: The cluster joins neutral amino acid import (glutamine, leucine, isoleucine, alanine, phenylalanine) with thyroid hormone transport and generation. The link is that thyroid hormones are amino-acid-derived and enter cells through amino acid-type carriers such as LAT and MCT transporters, while iodide transport by NIS (SLC5A5, whose defect causes thyroid dyshormonogenesis) supplies iodine for hormone synthesis. The cluster is about solute carriers that move amino acids and iodothyronines and how they support thyroid hormone supply and action.

theme: Rho family GTPase cycles and actin remodeling
story: The centre is the Rho family of small GTPases (RHOA/B/C/D/F/G/J/U/V, RAC1-3, CDC42, RND2/3) and their activation-inactivation cycles. Their effectors (formins, WASP/WAVE and Arp2/3, IQGAPs, PAKs) remodel actin into lamellipodia and filopodia and turn over focal adhesions, with G beta-gamma input to CDC42 and Ral signaling as related branches. The cluster describes how Rho GTPases control actin structure and cell motility.

theme: IL-10 and IL-12 family cytokine signaling
story: The centre is signaling by the IL-10 family (IL-10, IL-20 family) and the IL-12 family (IL-12, IL-23, IL-27, IL-35), which share receptor chains and JAK-STAT signaling. IL-12 and IL-23 promote inflammatory T-cell responses, whereas IL-10, IL-27, IL-35 and IL-37 dampen inflammation, matched by regulation of IL-10 production and negative regulation of inflammation to wounding. The cluster describes the cytokine network that sets the balance between inflammatory and regulatory immune responses.
